description: List the operational queue (bugs, feature requests, errors, alerts, measurement plans) in work order — highest priority first, oldest first within a priority. PAGING: `limit` (page size, 1–500) is REQUIRED — the call fails without it. Start at `offset: 0` and add `limit` to `offset` for the next page; a page shorter than `limit` is the last one. FILTERS (all optional, combined with AND, applied before paging): `type` = bug | feature_request | error | alert | measure_plan; `status` = open | in_progress | investigating_by_ai | blocked | ready_for_qa | resolved | wont_fix | pending_approval | unresolved | all — DEFAULTS TO `unresolved` (omitted = items still being worked: open, in_progress, blocked, ready_for_qa…; no resolved or wont_fix ones). Pass `status: "all"` to include resolved and wont_fix too (pending_approval is only returned when asked for exactly); `priority` = critical | high | medium | nice_to_have; `owner` = a person (id, email or name) or an agent (connector id, name or handle, e.g. "Claude"); `scope: "ready"` = what to work on now — open items nobody is working (no open run) that are unowned or were reopened after an earlier run. Use `scope: "ready"` to pick the next item, then `ops_ack` it.

limit.description: Page size — max items to return (1–500). A page shorter than `limit` is the last one.

offset.description: Number of items to skip before the page starts. Defaults to 0. The order is stable, so `offset += limit` walks the queue page by page.

owner.description: Narrow to items owned by one person OR one agent. Matches a person by `users.id`, email, or display name, and an agent by connector id, display name, or kebab-case handle — e.g. `owner=Claude` or `owner=alice@acme.dev`. Case-insensitive exact match.

anyOf.description: Triage priority of a queue item. The lowest tier is `nice_to_have` (not `low`) — carried over from the feature-request "importance" scale this priority set replaced.

priority.description: Filter by triage priority, or `all` (the default). Items with no priority set are returned only under `all`.

qaQuestions.description: `open` narrows to the items with at least one unanswered QA question — the backlog QA answers first (read each with `ops get`, answer with `ops qa-questions answer`). `all` (the default) applies no such narrowing.

scope.description: `ready` narrows to the items ready to be picked up right now: status `open`, no open run (nobody has acked it and is still working), and either unowned (no person and no agent) or reopened (sent back to `open` after an earlier run finished). Leave `status` unset with it. `all` (the default) applies no such narrowing.

anyOf.description: Lifecycle status of a queue item. The working flow is `open` → `in_progress` → `ready_for_qa` → `resolved` (or `wont_fix`, terminal from any earlier stage). `blocked` marks an item that can't progress until an external dependency clears — a working state a human sets and clears. `ready_for_qa` is what a developer sets once a fix lands; `resolved` is the QA sign-off, normally flipped in the dashboard after verification — set it directly from code only when the fix has been verified end-to-end. `investigating_by_ai` is a system-owned display state — set when the AI agent (Jarvis) picks an item up to investigate, never chosen by a human — so it is shown but not offered as a manual choice. `pending_approval` is the one human-gated holding state: it parks an item OUT of the work queue until a human promotes it to `open` in the dashboard, so `GET /api/admin/ops` excludes it under `status=all`/default and returns it only when requested as an exact `status`. It covers untriaged inbound that must never be auto-implemented — connector requests filed from a customer's connectors panel, and questions funnelled in from the "Stuck in onboarding?" assistant — where approving means flipping the status to `open`. Two earlier values were removed in favour of this single gate: `triage` (the onboarding-help bucket, now `pending_approval`) and `triaged` (a redundant "looked at but not started" step, now plain `open`).

status.description: Filter by one lifecycle status, `unresolved` for every status that is not `resolved` or `wont_fix`, or `all` for every status. Defaults to `all` over HTTP; the CLI and MCP tool default to `unresolved`, so pass `all` there to include resolved and won't-fix items. The human-gated holding state (`pending_approval`) is excluded from `unresolved` and `all`, and returned only when requested as the exact status.

anyOf.description: Queue item type. `bug` and `feature_request` are user-fileable; `error`, `alert`, and `measure_plan` tickets are auto-filed by the platform.

type.description: Filter by item type, or `all` (the default). Every type a returned item can carry is filterable, including the auto-filed ones.

name: ops_list
